evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.142: ad pulsandōs verberandōsque hominēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of knocking at a door (ōstium pulsāre) and of hitting people.

evidence: Quint. 2.8.13: pugnō ferīre vel calce (Lewis & Short)
Hor. C. 1.1.36: sublīmī feriam sīdera vertice
terms.comment: No perfect: percussī serves (Lewis & Short, after Varro).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.279: cum Catō percussus esset ab eō, quī arcam ferēbat (Lewis & Short)
Ter. Ad. 562: nōn puduisse verberāre hominem senem

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, intransitive: active in form, passive in sense
terms.register: vōx plērumque cōmica: Plaut., Ter.; in ōrātiōne solūtā rārior
evidence: Ter. Ad. 213: ego vāpulandō, ille verberandō
terms.comment: The partner of verberō: verberat, he beats; vāpulat, he gets beaten.

phrases.latin: ut Cratēs, cum indoctum puerum vīdisset, paedagōgum ejus percussit
phrases.english: as Crates, when he saw an ignorant boy, struck the boy’s tutor

phrases.latin: Ego vāpulandō, ille verberandō, ūsque ambō dēfessī sumus.
phrases.english: I with being beaten, he with beating, we’re both worn out.
